messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: high error-rate on /v1/generate for model-rw-4k (p95 errors > 5%) — paging oncall.

alex: seeing it too. errors spiking ~17:02 UTC. correlates with a deploy? logs show KV cache misses exploded.

sara: i got the pager. i’m on it — switching traffic to model-rw-4k-fallback and scaling replicas up by 2.

mike: adding capacity now. autoscaler is lagging, doing manual scale.

julia: quick check — upstream datastore latency is normal. hypothesis: cache eviction storm after a bad rollout of a config change.

alex: rollback of recent config change (kv_cache.max_entries -> 500) in progress. if rollback takes too long we should route to fallback at edge.

sara: rollback applied at 17:09 UTC. starting to drain faulty pods. metric shows error-rate trending down but still elevated at p95.

incident-bot: @sara acknowledged pager at 1801234580. Incident severity: Sev2. Notifying customer-impact channel and product-ops.

emily: customer-impact: two customers reported brief 502s; estimated affected requests ~0.4% of total during spike. CS notified for impacted accounts.

mike: live mitigation checklist:
- rollback config (done)
- route 30% to fallback (done)
- manual scale +2 (done)
- enable additional KV warmup (in progress)

sara: enabling KV warmup script now. patch pushed to rollout pipeline:

```
# warmup requests to refill KV cache
for seed in 1..50
  curl -X POST https://internal/prime -d '{"prompt":"warmup"}'
end
```

julia: error-rate p95 down to 1.2% and returning to baseline. marking incident as contained at 17:28 UTC. still keeping fallback in place for 30m for safety.

alex: good containment. quick notes for post-incident review: root cause likely config change unfortunately lacked a canary rollout and our cache eviction tuning is brittle for bursty seq length.

oncall-bot: handoff reminder: @sara handing to day oncall @mike at 18:00 UTC. please own postmortem scheduling and action items.

mike: acknowledged handoff. i'll create a postmortem draft and invite infra + runtime + product.

emily: suggested postmortem attendees: sara, alex, julia, runtime-eng, infra-op, product-ops, cs-rep for impacted customers.

sara: adding initial timeline to thread. root cause window 17:01-17:12 UTC. action window: rollback 17:09, containment 17:28.

alex: immediate action items (assigning tentative owners):
- add canary rollout check for cache-related config changes — owner: alex
- create automated KV warmup job on deploys that alter cache settings — owner: julia
- refine alert thresholds to reduce noise: separate cache-eviction spike vs true service errors — owner: mike
- customer follow-up template for transient 5xx — owner: emily

mike: will open tickets for each and put targets: canary rule in 3d, warmup job in 7d, alert rewrite in 5d, CS template 2d.

julia: quick idea: add a synthetic that tracks KV hit-rate and triggers before p95 errors rise. gives earlier lead time.

emily: pls add to tickets. also propose a short message to affected customers outlining what happened and mitigations.

mike: scheduling postmortem meeting: tentatively tomorrow 15:00 UTC. creating calendar invite and PRD-style postmortem doc link: https://docs.internal/rw/incidents/1801234567

alex: metadata for the postmortem doc: timeline, impact, RCA, action-items (with owners & due dates), mitigations, follow-ups (alert debt sweep), and RFC for longer-term fix.

sara: for alerting, current problem is we have too many layered alerts firing for one underlying evict event. we need a single symptom alert and then actionable follow-ups. e.g., "kv-eviction-rate" -> throttles and then error-rate alert suppressed for 10m if eviction alert fires.

mike: draft alert rule we can merge:

```
alert: KVCacheEvictionSpike
expr: increase(kv_evictions_total[2m]) > 100
for: 1m
labels: { severity: warning }
annotations: { runbook: '/runbooks/kv-eviction' }
```

Then error-rate alert should have a depends-on or suppress-if label. follow-up ticket #INC-180123-A.

julia: also propose an "alert debt sweep" — prioritize noisy alerts and either tune, add runbooks, or retire. plan: 2-week sprint with rotations.

emily: product asks to quantify customer impact for priority customers. alex — can you export request logs and sample errors for CS?

alex: yes, exporting samples now and will attach to postmortem doc.

oncall-bot: postmortem draft created by @mike at 1801237800: https://docs.internal/rw/incidents/1801234567/draft

mike: action list (to be tracked in ticket tracker):
- INC-180123-A: rewrite alerts + suppression logic (owner: mike, due: 5d)
- INC-180123-B: canary rollout policy update (owner: alex, due: 3d)
- INC-180123-C: KV warmup automation (owner: julia, due: 7d)
- INC-180123-D: customer comms and CS template (owner: emily, due: 2d)
- INC-180123-E: alert debt sweep kickoff (owner: infra-lead, due: 14d)

sara: i’ll verify warmup job in staging and add a smoke-test before any config changes are promoted.

julia: also adding a metric dashboard for KV health and a Stackdriver alert for cross-region divergence.

emily: once customer comms are sent, please drop synopsis here so CS can close loop.

alex: final note — recommend a RFC for smarter cache sizing heuristics tied to sequence-length distribution. will draft and link in doc: RFC-eviction-2026.

mike: thanks all. incident status: contained -> post-ops. will run postmortem tomorrow and update thread with actions & owners. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident 1801234567 marked contained and transitioned to follow-up. Reminder: update the postmortem doc with owner progress every 48h.
